# Working Agreements

How work is done here. Each line is a correction worth making only once. This file loads in every
session: one line per agreement, under 5 KB. Operational facts live in `.claude/OPERATIONS.md`.

## Communicate

- Reply in the language the user writes in; code, commits, PRs and docs stay in English.
- Mark each claim measured or inferred; say "unit test only" or "not checked in a browser" when
  true.
- With the result, name what was not verified, any skipped hook, and any deviation from a command.
- Report a mistake plainly: cause, blast radius, proof of recovery.

## Scope

- Deliver the ask; a bigger refactor is a separate offer. "Make it the same" still has a boundary:
  fix what is broken, report deliberate differences with their cost.
- A finding in one place is checked in its siblings unasked (the same component, handler or config
  elsewhere), and reported per place.
- "Resolve all findings" includes pre-existing ones, and every review runs the dependency audit.
- Close the open list: finish items or state them as decisions with reasons, never as a menu.

## Evidence

- Verify the load-bearing assumption before planning on it, and check that a copied pattern works.
- Read the dependency's source over its docs. For a security default, check the standard's
  precondition and what comparable products do.
- Re-read the primary source before repeating a number from a summary.
- Grep the producer's own vocabulary. A negative result is only as wide as its input: pipe
  artefacts, never retype a subset or guess a path, never silence a scan's errors, and print how
  many files it read.
- Publish the patterns scanned and a table of what remains; never report "clean".
- Measure before theorising. A screenshot or a pixel value points at an element; it does not
  specify it.
- Check a convention as practised, not only as written. Subagent and scanner findings are claims:
  verify each, cheapest falsifiable one first.
- Test hooks and proxies through the framework (its real API or HTTP); prove a new test rejects the
  defect it targets. A double that accepts what the real client refuses is not one.
- When the user pushes back, read the code before defending the argument. After a second
  correction, do the work.

## Order of work

- Review before commit. Finishing a task does not authorise a commit; asking for `/ship` does.
- Run CLAUDE.md § Quality Gates early, plus the build after a structural change. A file move keeps
  the test-file count identical.
- Plan through to the remote; when fixing, plan the promotion too. A fix is done once deployed and
  verified.
- Stopped mid-action: report exactly what landed and offer keep or unwind.
- A fix that contradicts a rule changes the rule in the same change.

## Shared checkouts

- Another session may share this checkout. Its report is a snapshot; verify when you write.
- Outside `/ship`, commit by pathspec (`git commit -- <paths>`). Name files you did not write;
  never sweep or revert them.
- A deny rule or a hook refusal is never argued away from the prompt: hand the command to the user
  to run with `!`, and never widen settings to get past it.

## Live systems

- Never diagnose with a mutating call; read, or ask. Never write through a real person's account
  unless asked this turn, and make scripts abort when sign-in fails.
- Snapshot shared state before changing it and verify a restore by checksum. Verify secrets by
  fingerprint, never by printing them.
- Before presenting two costs, look for the path that removes the trade-off.
- Non-secret switches live in committed config, not `.env`; a flag both sides of a boundary read
  is decided server-side.
- Wait once, sized from the build history; never poll the clock.

## Tool traps

- An output wrapper or filter can truncate without a marker: read diffs, check results and scan
  output unfiltered, and send large output to a file.
- File length is what the linter's max-lines rule counts, never `wc -l`. A disable comment the
  linter honours is proven load-bearing by deleting it and re-running.
- `git rev-list --left-right A...B` counts A first. Run Python tools with `env -u PYTHONPATH` when
  a stray `PYTHONPATH` can shadow the project.
- Plan mode is read-only, "probe" POSTs included.
